title: Many come
hookLine: the fire-worshipers, the kings, the friends (Buddhacarita 16)

lines: A YOUNG MAN WAKES AT NIGHT.
HE WALKS OUT, AND FRIENDS FOLLOW.
cards: A rich young man wakes in the middle of the night in a beautiful house. The lamps are still burning. The musicians who played for him have fallen asleep where they sat, sprawled and snoring.
Suddenly he sees it all as ugly and sad. If that sounds familiar, it should: it's the prince's night, a few cantos back, happening to someone else. His name is Yasas.
He walks out of the house in distress, and he finds the Buddha. And after him, the poem says, his friends come too.

teach.b: Canto sixteen is a canto of arrivals. First, the friends. Yasas is taught, and goes forth.
His friends hear what he's done and come to see for themselves. The teaching travels the way news often travels: one friend tells another. Second, the fire-worshipers.

At Uruvilva lives a well-known ascetic of the Kashyapa family, a keeper of sacred fires, with his brothers and a crowd of followers. The Buddha asks to spend the night in the hall where the fire is kept.
There's a fierce serpent in there, they warn him. He goes in anyway, and in the morning the serpent lies calm in his bowl.
Even so, the story has the eldest brother hold on to his pride for a while, until at last he yields.

He and his followers give up their fire rites, and the tradition says they threw their fire gear into the river. Downstream, his brothers see it floating past, and come upriver to find out what happened.
To these fire-keepers the Buddha speaks in their own language: everything is burning. The eye is burning, the ear, the mind, with the fires of desire, anger and delusion.
People who tended fire all their lives hear about a fire they can put out.

teach.h: A KING, AND A PROMISE KEPT.
teach.b: Fourth, the king. In Rajagriha, King Bimbisara, who once offered the young wanderer half a kingdom, hears he has come back.
The prince had promised to return once he found what he was looking for, and he keeps the promise. The king comes out to listen, and is moved. Friends, fire-keepers, a king.

how: The Fire Sermon is still chanted and taught in Theravada communities, and in some communities monasteries and temples receive newcomers, from curious visitors to people asking to ordain, with a simple welcome and a place to sit.

o: arrivals: friends, fire-keepers and a king join
a festival where pilgrims crowd a temple
a sermon preached to a huge crowd at once

games.q: the arrivals in canto sixteen: tap the pairs.
p: wakes at night and walks out
the serpent in the fire hall
lies calm in his bowl by morning

s: Yasas's night echoes the prince's own night in the palace
he wakes among sleeping musicians and sees it all as sad, then walks out.
the eldest Kashyapa gives up his pride the moment the serpent is calmed
the story has him hold on to his pride for a while before he yields.
the fire sermon is about a fire you tend
it's about the fires of desire, anger and delusion, and putting them out.

games.q: you're a younger Kashyapa brother, living downstream. one morning your elder brother's fire gear floats past in the river. what do you do?
o: fish it out and keep it.
assume an accident and carry on.
go upriver to find out what happened.
games.why: they go upriver to find out, and they too stay to hear the Buddha. one brother's change becomes the family's.

practice: Bring to mind someone new somewhere you already belong, a coworker, a neighbor, a new face in a class or a place of worship, and picture the door they walked through as it looks from their side.
Hold them there with a plain, friendly wish, and rest with the breath.

wordCard.voice: Many come. Yasas and his friends, the Kashyapa brothers with their fire, and King Bimbisara, all arriving in one canto. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: everything is burning. And a fire that burns can also be put out. Day seven hundred nineteen.

sources.ref: Vinaya, Mahavagga 1 (Yasa; the Kassapas; the fire sermon; Bimbisara)
Samyutta Nikaya 35.28 (Adittapariyaya Sutta, the fire sermon)
